title: Local models of integral constructible complexes and their cohomology
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k_0$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and a chosen uniformizer $\pi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use the completed coefficient sheaf $\mathcal O_{E,X}$ of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and the bounded-constructible cohomology definition of $\Dbc$ in [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Let $K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$.

1. There is a finite stratification of $X$ such that on each stratum $S$,
   pro-étale locally on $S$, $K|_S$ is the completion
   $\widehat{\underline{M^\bullet}}=M^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_{E,S}$
   of a bounded complex $M^\bullet$ of finite free $\mathcal O_E$-modules, with
   differentials given by matrices over $\mathcal O_E$.
2. Each cohomology sheaf $H^q(K)$ is derived complete, lies in
   $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$, and on each stratum of (1) is pro-étale locally the
   completion of the finitely generated $\mathcal O_E$-module $H^q(M^\bullet)$.
3. Every truncation $\tau_{\le q}K$, $\tau_{\ge q}K$ lies in
   $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$.

proof.text: Put $R=\mathcal O_E$, $\pi=\pi_E$ and $B_T=\mathcal O_{E,T}=\varprojlim_n(R/\pi^n)_T$. The Noetherian scheme setting and coefficient identification are [sk-lem-integral-models]. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $R$ is a local PID with maximal ideal $\pi R$, hence Noetherian (each ideal has one generator). By [lem-sfb-integers-profinite-tower](1), the reduction map $R\to\varprojlim_nR/\pi^n$ is a ring isomorphism, so $R$ is $(\pi)$-adically complete.

source.place: Clause (1), coefficient hypotheses for the adic local-structure theorem

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-integral-cohomological-adic-criterion](1)$\Rightarrow$(2), $K$ is locally derived $(\pi)$-complete and its residue reduction is pulled back from a bounded étale constructible complex of finite Tor amplitude. These are condition (a) of [lem-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect]. Apply (a)$\Rightarrow$(b), with the ring and scheme hypotheses of step 1, to obtain strata and charts with $K|_U\simeq B_U\otimes_R P^\bullet$ for bounded finite projective scalar complexes.

Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-projective-complex-matrix-model] to each scalar complex $P^\bullet$ of step 2 over the DVR of step 1. It gives a bounded finite free matrix complex $M^\bullet\simeq P^\bullet$ with the same support bounds. Termwise scalar extension carries this complex isomorphism to the chart, giving (1).

source.place: Clause (1), finite free models over the discrete valuation ring; Stacks Tag 0AUW(3)

proof.text: By [sk-def-sfb-constructible], $H^q(K)[0]$ is bounded constructible: its other cohomology sheaves are zero, with zero finite constant model. Apply [sk-lem-integral-models](2) to this degree-zero object. It is derived complete in the canonical derived-limit sense of [sk-def-pe-derived-completion], proving the first assertions of (2).

source.place: Clause (2), *Completeness*; realized by sk-lem-integral-models(2) applied to the degree-zero object H^q(K)[0] instead of Stacks Tags 0990 and 099Q(5)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-local-integral-perfect-model-cohomology] to $g:S\hookrightarrow X$, each original chart $U$, and $P^\bullet$ of step 2. It gives $H^q(K)|_U\simeq B_U\otimes_R H^q(P^\bullet)$ with finitely presented scalar cohomology. The complex isomorphism $M^\bullet\simeq P^\bullet$ of step 3 identifies their cohomology, giving $H^q(K)|_U\simeq B_U\otimes_R H^q(M^\bullet)$ with finitely generated scalar cohomology. Together with step 4 this proves (2) on the original strata and charts.

source.place: Clause (2), local cohomology of finite free models; Stacks Tags 093J, 093M, 00IK

proof.text: By [def-kun-truncations], the two good truncations retain $H^i(K)$ respectively for $i\leq q$ and $i\geq q$, and are zero elsewhere. Both lists vanish outside a finite interval and are constructible (including zero). By [sk-def-sfb-constructible] both truncations lie in $\Dbc$, proving (3).

source.place: Clause (3), elementary truncation argument using the bounded-constructible definition

proof_origin.place: Clauses (1)–(3), using Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.6.11 and the existing integral cohomological criterion
